{{Quote|It's unusual for an animated film, because it's not really like say ''Beowulf'' and it's not a Pixar movie, so it kind of falls in between in this funny world where ''Star Wars'' is, which is kind of hard-edged but not really, sort of on the verge of PG-13, flips over once in a while, but sort of the high end of PG.|George Lucas|<ref name="CWQA">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news/news20080317.html|text=George Lucas Talks ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''}}</ref>}}
'''''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''''' is a [[2008]] animated feature film directed by [[Dave Filoni]] and [[Wikipedia:Executive producer|executive produced]] by [[George Lucas]] as well as the first Star Wars animated film made. The plot focuses on a struggle between the [[Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]—each vying for [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba the Hutt's]] permission to use [[Hutt Space]]'s [[Hyperspace route|trade routes]]. In an attempt to gain Jabba's favor, [[Sith Lord]] and Separatist leader [[Count]] [[Dooku]] kidnaps Jabba's son [[Rotta]], in hopes of framing the Republic's [[Jedi Order]] as the true captors.

The film is set during the three-year time period between the films [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] (2002) and [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] (2005). ''The Clone Wars'' served as an introduction to the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|animated series of the same name]] that premiered on [[Cartoon Network]] on [[October 3]], 2008. Lucas was inspired to make the movie while reviewing footage from the series and described the film as "almost an afterthought." The film was released [[August 15]], 2008.

The film was a box office success, and grossed $68.3 million worldwide against an $8.5 million budget,<ref name="TCWOCE">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Collector's Edition|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' – The Official Collector's Edition]]</ref> and earned $14.6 million during its opening weekend.

The film chronologically takes place between the [[The Clone Wars: Season One|Season One]] episode "[[The Hidden Enemy]]" and [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|Season Three]] episode "[[Clone Cadets]]."

==Plot summary==
The film begins with a narrator explaining the state of the [[Clone Wars]]. The Separatists control the majority of the [[Hyperspace route|hyperlanes]], leaving Republic forces stranded in different parts of the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]]. An [[Trident-class assault ship|octopus-like craft]] heads for [[Tatooine]] to capture [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba]] the [[Hutt]]'s son [[Rotta]] as part of a plan to make the Hutts join the [[Clone Wars]].

Meanwhile, a fierce battle is taking place on the crystalline [[planet]] of [[Christophsis]] between the Republic's very limited [[Grand Army of the Republic|clone army]] and the [[Retail Caucus]] forces. With the help of [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Anakin Skywalker]], [[Rex]], and [[Cody]], the clones steadily advance on the Separatists' forces, gaining the Republic an early victory. It doesn't last long, though, as the droid army under General [[Whorm Loathsom|Loathsom]] soon returns for more bloodshed. With no communications or the ability to fly in reinforcements, the fate of the few remaining clone soldiers are in the hands of Obi-Wan and Anakin. A shuttle soon comes with an important delivery; thinking it's reinforcements, the Jedi are suprised to find just a young [[Padawan]] named [[Ahsoka Tano]], who insists that she has been sent by Master [[Yoda]] to serve as Anakin's Padawan.

The battle resumes, with [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist]] forces advancing behind an expanding shield which the Republic's artillery is unable to penetrate. Tasked with taking down the [[Deflector shield|deflector]] shield, Anakin and Ahsoka succeed in penetrating the enemy lines, using all their stealth, cunning and ability to improvise, while Obi-Wan stalls for time by holding a fake surrender negotiation with Loathsom.

Soon after the [[Battle of Christophsis|final victory]] for the Republic on [[Christophsis]], Master Yoda arrives with the urgent message that a mysterious group of renegades has kidnapped Jabba's son, and it's up to Anakin, Ahsoka, Rex, and the clones to rescue him and bring him back home safely. Obi-Wan flies to [[Tatooine]] to assure Jabba that Rotta will be returned safely and to secure a promise by the Hutts to use their trading routes for safe passage within the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]].

After briefing in a Republic flagship, Anakin's forces descend through the clouds of the jungle planet of [[Teth]] for one of the many natural stone pillars which litter the landscape. Under heavy fire, Anakin, Ahsoka and Rex storm the [[B'omarr Order Monastery|monastery]] atop the pillar and find Rotta, who has gotten sick, only to be caught in an elaborate trap: Count [[Dooku]] has staged the kidnapping himself in order to blacklist the [[Jedi]] among the Hutts. First he has the Jedi retrieve the young [[Hutt]] to secure fake evidence and then [[Asajj Ventress]], as the overseer of the operation, is charged with either retrieving or killing the young Huttlet.

While quarreling all the while about the proper procedure, yet slowly gaining respect of one another, Anakin and Ahsoka manage to escape the trap along with [[R2-D2]] and hijack a derelict [[Twilight|transport]], which they use to travel to Tatooine. Ahsoka uses medicine onboard to treat the sick Huttlet. Obi-Wan, alerted by Anakin, arrives just in time to relieve Rex and the rest of his forces and engages Ventress in combat where he manages to defeat her, though Ventress flees in the face of capture.

In the meantime, [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Amidala]] learns of Anakin's mission. Worried about him, she decides to contact Jabba's uncle, [[Ziro Desilijic Tiure|Ziro the Hutt]], who lives in a shady part of [[Coruscant]]. The Hutt strangely refuses to cooperate, and soon Padmé finds out why: Ziro has actually conspired with Dooku to engineer the downfall of his nephew to seize the power over the Hutt clans for himself. Padmé is discovered and detained, but a chance call by [[C-3PO]] enables her to summon help, and Ziro is soon arrested by the [[Coruscant Guard]].

Upon their arrival on Tatooine, Anakin and Ahsoka are attacked by [[IG-100 MagnaGuard|MagnaGuards]] and shot down. Faced with a long way across desert sands and relentless opponents, Anakin devises a ruse; when Dooku corners Anakin, the pack he is carrying is revealed to contain merely rocks. Ahsoka and R2 travel with Rotta to Jabba's palace unmolested, but just as they near it, Ahsoka is ambushed by three MagnaGuards, whom she narrowly defeats. But as Anakin and Ahsoka enter the palace one after another, they are threatened with execution by Jabba's men even though Rotta is safely returned. Padmé calls just in time to convince Jabba of his uncle's duplicity, while Anakin and Ahsoka are triumphantly retrieved by Obi-Wan, Yoda, Cody and the clones. Dooku tells Sidious about his failure but Sidious tells Dooku that the tide of war still turned in their favor according with Sidious' master plan as Jabba allowed the Republic to use the Hutt Cartel hyperspace lanes.

==Development==
''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' was designed to serve as both a stand-alone story and a lead-in to the weekly [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|animated TV series of the same name]].<ref name="OfficialBlog-Report from Wonder-Con: Lucasfilm Presentation Part 3">{{OfficialBlog|url=2008/02/23/report-from-wonder-con-lucasfilm-presentation-part-3|text=Report from Wonder-Con: Lucasfilm Presentation (Part 3)}}</ref> [[George Lucas]] had the idea for a film after viewing some of the already completed footage on the big screen.<ref name="CWQA" /> [[Warner Bros.]] had tracked the series' development from the beginning, and Lucas decided on a theatrical launch after viewing some footage,<ref name="aswv">{{WebCite|url=http://variety.com/2008/digital/markets-festivals/animated-star-wars-to-hit-theaters-1117980757|text=Animated 'Star Wars' to hit theaters|author=Garrett, Diane|date=2008-02-11|archivedate=20160123042209}}</ref> and deciding, "This is so beautiful, why don't we just go and use the crew and make a feature?" Lucas described the film was "almost an afterthought."<ref name="EW Lucas Q&A">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/article/2008/03/18/george-lucas-star-wars-plan|text=George Lucas on 'Star Wars', Indiana Jones|author=Rich, Joshua|work=[[Wikipedia:Entertainment Weekly|Entertainment Weekly]]|archivedate=20200614175153}}</ref> [[Howard Roffman]], president of [[Lucas Licensing]], said of the decision, "Sometimes George works in strange ways."<ref name="NYT0701">{{WebCite|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/07/01/business/media/01adco.html?_r=1&oref=slogin|text=The Force lives on, as do the toys|author=Quenqua, Douglas|date=2008-07-01|archivedate=20200614174947}}</ref> Producer [[Catherine Winder]] said the sudden decision added to an already large challenge of establishing a show "of this sophistication and complexity,"<ref name="Georgia">{{WebCite|url=https://www.straight.com/article-158377/clone-wars-galactic-task|text=Clone Wars proved a galactic task for production team|author=Lupick, Travis|date=2008-08-21|archivedate=20200503040610}}</ref> but she felt it was a good way to start the series, and she felt budgetary constraints forced the production team to think outside the box in a positive way.<ref name="Georgia" /> One of the film's main plot threads—the kidnapping of [[Rotta|Jabba the Hutt's son]]—was inspired by the film [[Wikipedia:Shogun's Shadow|''Shogun's Shadow'']].<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.newsarama.com/1064-clone-wars-weekly-dispatch-writer-henry-gilroy-p3.html|text=Clone Wars Weekly Dispatch - Writer Henry Gilroy, p3|author=Fritz, Steve|date=2008-09-19|archivedate=20160410114028}}</ref>

The main part of the film was composed of three episodes with similar titles originally meant to form a trilogy: "Castle of Deception," "Castle of Doom"<ref name="pablo">{{JCFCite|url=posts/29437817|board=Live Action, Clone Wars & Classics|thread=The Clone Wars- Episode 106: Downfall of a Droid Discussion Thread (Spoilers Allowed)|user=[[Pablo Hidalgo|Pabawan]]|date=2008-11-11|time=6:23 PM|archivedate=20160427093053}}</ref> and "Castle of Salvation,"<ref name="bullockint">{{Blogspot|subdomain=bullockartworks|url=2008/10/dave-bullock-clone-wars-interview.html|name=Bullock Art Works|text=Bullock Art Works: Dave Bullock Clone Wars Interview}}</ref> while a standalone episode "The New Padawan," which was developed later in the production as a flashback episode during the series, became the opening sequence of the movie, eventually leading to the introduction of [[Ahsoka Tano]].<ref name="db">{{DB|location|christophsis|Christophsis}}</ref>

[[Lucasfilm Animation]] used [[Wikipedia:Autodesk|Autodesk]] [[Wikipedia:Software|software]] to animate the film. The [[Wikipedia:Maya (software)|Maya]] [[Wikipedia:3D modeler|3D modeling]] program was used to create highly detailed worlds, characters and creatures.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://tradingmarkets.com/.site/news/Stock%20News/1845253|text=Autodesk Maya software serves as animation platform for new ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' animated feature film and TV series|date=2008-08-26|archivedate=20080916095902}}</ref> The film's animation style was designed to pay homage to the stylized looks of both [[Wikipedia:Japan|Japanese]] [[Wikipedia:Anime|anime]] and [[Wikipedia:Manga|manga]], and the [[Wikipedia:Supermarionation|supermarionation]] of the [[Wikipedia:England|British]] [[1960s]] series [[Wikipedia:Thunderbirds|''Thunderbirds'']]. At a [[Cartoon Network]]-hosted discussion, Lucas said did not want the ''Clone Wars'' film or television series to look like such movies as [[Wikipedia:Beowulf (2007 film)|''Beowulf'']] because he wanted a stylized look rather than a realistic one, and he did not want it to look like the popular [[Wikipedia:Pixar|Pixar]] films, such as [[Wikipedia:The Incredibles|''The Incredibles'']] because he wanted the film and characters to have a unique style.<ref name="Broadcasting & Cable">{{WebCite|url=http://www.broadcastingcable.com/index.asp?layout=blog&blog_id=1380000138&blog_post_id=1960024396|text=George Lucas Talks 'Clone Wars'|author=Weprin, Alex|date=2008-04-03|archivedate=20080408153204}}</ref> Lucas also decided to create the animated film and series from a live-action perspective, which Winder said set it apart from other CGI films because it "meant using long camera shots, aggressive lighting techniques, and relying on editing instead of storyboards."<ref name="Georgia" /> Animators also reviewed designs from the [[Star Wars: Clone Wars|original 2003 ''Clone Wars'' series]] when creating the animation style for the film and the new series.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://extranews.net/news.php?nid=4031|text=Hispanic animator helps create new ''Star Wars'' universe|author=Martinez, Kiko|date=2008-08-27|archivedate=20080915010715}}</ref>

The film's music was composed by [[Kevin Kiner]].<ref name="soundtrack">{{SWArchive|url=vault/collecting/news20080709.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Soundtrack}}</ref> Steward Lee is a storyboard artist.<ref name="aswv" /> When it was decided to produce the film, Lucasfilm contacted all the major film ''Star Wars'' actors to see who was interested in voicing their characters for ''The Clone Wars''.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.ugo.com/ugo/html/article/?id=558&sectionId=2|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars Interviews|archivedate=20080820043432}}</ref> In the end, [[Anthony Daniels]], [[Matthew Wood]], [[Christopher Lee]] and [[Samuel L. Jackson]] returned to voice their respective characters.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/news/movies/la-et-lucas7-2008may07,0,3749545.story|text=George Lucas: 'Star Wars' won't go beyond Darth Vader|author=Boucher, Geoff|date=2008-05-07|archivedate=20200825174350}}</ref> Several voice actors also reprised their roles from the [[Star Wars: Clone Wars|2003 series]].

Warner Bros. Animation, [[Industrial Light & Magic]], Production I.G, [[Polygon Pictures]], and CGCG contributed some animation for the film.

==Release and reception==
{{Quote|This is a breakthrough project -- returning Star Wars to the big screen in a completely new way while beginning an exciting new chapter in George Lucas' legendary saga. We immediately felt that it would be a fantastic theatrical event and are thrilled to be bringing it to moviegoers.|Dan Fellman, Warner Bros. Pictures President of Domestic Distribution|<ref name="ann" />}}
At Hasbro's fall 2007 analyst event, it was announced that ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' would have a "theatrical launch" on [[August 8]], 2008, with it beginning to be shown on TV during that fall.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://phx.corporate-ir.net/phoenix.zhtml?c=68329&p=irol-IRHome|text=Hasbro Fall 2007 Analyst Event|archivedate=20060208014918}}</ref> Although Lucasfilm had previously announced that it would produce an animated feature film in 2008,<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://content.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,1708826-2,00.html|text=Fantasy League|author=Kingsbury, Kathleen|date=2008-01-31|archivedate=20161107124047}}</ref> when initially asked for confirmation, an LFL representative replied that "It's one of the many things being discussed but we have no decisions yet. For us it's all about finding a creative way to launch a creative TV series."<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/latestnews/story/Animated_Clone_Wars_Theatrical_Release_Possible_110151.asp|text=Animated Clone Wars Theatrical Release Possible?|archivedate=20071116131012}}</ref>

At ToyFare 2008, a LEGO official announced that an animated feature film would be released in the UK in September 2008,<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.jedinews.co.uk/features/feature.aspx?featureID=6|text=Jedi News at the UK Toy Fair 2008: Hasbro, LEGO and lots more!|archivedate=20080208180443}}</ref> and would be made up of the first three episodes of the series, with regular episodes airing later on television on an at-the-time unrevealed channel.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.action-figure.com/index.php?name=News&file=article&sid=22558&theme=Printer|text=Guess Which Line Hasbro Was Keeping The Press Away From?|author=Faulkner, Adrian|date=2008-01-30|archivedate=20090218122101}}</ref> It was officially announced on [[February 12]], 2008 that the feature film would be released in theaters on [[August 15]], 2008, with the TV series debuting in the fall.<ref name="ann" /> Warner Bros. showed a preview of the film in Las Vegas, Nevada on March 13, 2008.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.showest.com/filmexpo/photos/pdf/A_WB.pdf|text=WARNER BROS. PICTURES IS A "BIG" PRESENCE AT SHOWEST|date=2008-02-20|archivedate=20080517160152}}</ref> Lucas attended the event and held a question and answer session.<ref name="CWQA" /> The first theatrical trailer debuted on May 8, 2008 on five separate [[Wikipedia:Turner Broadcasting System|Turner Network]] channels.<ref name="SWArchive-The Trailer & Poster for Star Wars: The Clone Wars">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news/news20080506.html|text=The Trailer & Poster for ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''}}</ref> A second trailer was released in June 2008.<ref name="SW-The Clone Wars: Theatrical Trailer #2">{{SW|url=video/the-clone-wars-theatrical-trailer-2|text=The Clone Wars: Theatrical Trailer #2}}</ref>

The film premiered at [[Wikipedia:Grauman's Egyptian Theatre|Grauman's Egyptian Theatre]] on [[August 10]], 2008,<ref name="SWArchive-Star Wars: The Clone Wars To Premiere at Egyptian Theatre">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news20080709.html|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' To Premiere at Egyptian Theatre}}</ref> and was later screened on [[August 14]], 2008 at [[Wikipedia:Los Angeles, California|Los Angeles's]] [[Wikipedia:Nokia Theater|Nokia Theater]] accompanying a Lucasfilm VIP party with special guests John Knoll and Dave Filoni. SpikeTV producer Terry Minogue speculated that his channel would debut the film on television at some point after its theatrical release.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/latestnews/story/ForceCast_March_28_2008_113490.asp|text=Force-Cast: March 28, 2008|author=Swank, Jason|date=2008-03-28|archivedate=20170202105359}}</ref> The film had its US broadcast premiere on Cartoon Network on November 20, 2010.<ref name="SWArchive-See Where The Clone Wars Began This Saturday on Cartoon Network">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/moviecartoonnetwork/index.html|text=See Where ''The Clone Wars'' Began This Saturday on Cartoon Network}}</ref>

==Adaptations and tie-in media==
[[File:TCW_soundtrack.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Soundtrack for the film.]]
''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' merchandise was first released on [[July 26]], 2008. [[Hasbro]] released several 3 3/4-inch ''Clone Wars'' [[Wikipedia:Action figure|action figures]], an electronic clone trooper helmet, a customizable lightsaber, and an electronic [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer|AT-TE]].<ref name="OfficialBlog-Hasbro's Clone Wars figures at Toy Fair">{{OfficialBlog|url=2008/02/17/hasbros-clone-wars|text=Hasbro's ''Clone Wars'' figures at Toy Fair}}</ref> [[Wikipedia:Toys "R" Us|Toys "R" Us]] mounted digital clocks in all 585 of its stores that counted down to the release of the ''Clone Wars'' toys, and more than 225 of the stores opened at midnight for the debut of the ''Star Wars'' products. Two of the Toys "R" Us flagship outlets in [[Wikipedia:Mission Bay, San Diego, California|Mission Bay]], [[Wikipedia:San Diego, California|San Diego]], [[Wikipedia:California|California]] and [[Wikipedia:Times Square|Times Square]] in [[Wikipedia:Manhattan|Manhattan]], [[Wikipedia:New York City|New York City]] held costume and trivia contests on July 26 and gave away limited-edition ''Star Wars'' toys with every purchase. A section of the Toys "R" Us [[Wikipedia:Website|website]] was also dedicated to ''The Clone Wars''.<ref name="NYT0701" />

Due to the Lucas's sudden decision to make a ''Clone Wars'' film after viewing footage of the television show, Lucas Licensing did not have time to enter into agreements with previous ''Star Wars'' marketing partners like [[Wikipedia:Pepsi|Pepsi]], [[Wikipedia:Burger King|Burger King]] and [[Wikipedia:Kellogg Company|Kellogg's]], with which the [[Lucasfilm]] licensing company had a 10-year marketing plan for the other films; when questioned by [[Wikipedia:The New York Times|''The New York Times'']] for a ''Star Wars'' merchandising in July 2006, a Pepsi spokesperson was unaware a new ''Star Wars'' film was even being released. [[Wikipedia:Target Corporation|Target]] and [[Wikipedia:KB Toys|KB Toys]] also devoted shelf space for ''Clone Wars'' toys, but did not hold midnight releases or pursue the branding opportunities Toys "R" Us did. The [[Wikipedia:McDonald's|McDonald's]] [[Wikipedia:Fast food restaurant|fast food restaurant]] chain held its first ever [[Wikipedia:Happy Meal|Happy Meal]] promotion for a ''Star Wars'' movie starting on August 15. For four weeks, 18 exclusive toys came in specially designed Happy Meal boxes.<ref name="NYT0701" />

[[Wikipedia:DK Publishing|DK Publishing]] and [[Wikipedia:Penguin Group|Penguin Group]] released tie-in books, activities and other merchandise, including ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]'' (published by DK) and ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' (published by Puffin in the UK and by Grosset & Dunlap in the U.S). The publishers also released storybook, picture books and an activity book.<ref name="SWArchive-Penguin Group and DK Publishing to Publish Star Wars: The Clone Wars Books">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/young/news20080429.html|text=Penguin Group and DK Publishing to Publish ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Books}}</ref> At the [[Wikipedia:American International Toy Fair|American International Toy Fair]], [[LEGO]] announced a product line for the film and the TV series, to be released in July 2008 in the United States and August 2008 in the United Kingdom.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://gizmodo.com/357370/lego-new-clone-wars-sets-will-excite-whoever-gets-excited-by-clone-wars|text=LEGO new ''Clone Wars'' sets will excite whoever gets excited by ''Clone Wars''|date=2008-02-16|archivedate=20170705122851}}</ref> [[LucasArts]] adapted the movie into ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance]]'' for the [[Wikipedia:Nintendo DS|Nintendo DS]] and ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Lightsaber Duels]]'' for [[Wikipedia:Wii|Wii]].<ref name="LucasArts-The Clone Wars Official Site">{{LucasArts|url=games/theclonewars|text=''The Clone Wars''}}</ref> A reviewer from ''PocketGamer.co.uk'' said his expectations for ''Jedi Alliance'' were low due to poor ''Clone Wars'' movie reviews, but he found the game "a varied and well-paced experience."<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.pocketgamer.co.uk/r/DS/Star+Wars+The+Clone+Wars:+Jedi+Alliance/news.asp?c=8526|text=GC 2008: Hands on with ''Star Wars The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance''|author=Jordan, Jon|date=2008-08-24|archivedate=20170723105832}}</ref>

[[Dark Horse Comics]] published a six-issue digest-sized [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Slaves of the Republic|mini-series]]. [[Randy Stradley]], vice president of publishing for Dark Horse, said the sudden decision to release the ''Clone Wars'' film required the company to temporarily delay plans for two other ''Star Wars'' comic book series, [[Star Wars: Dark Times|''Dark Times'']] and [[Star Wars: Rebellion (comic series)|''Rebellion'']]. The ''Clone Wars'' comics did not receive the promotional campaign it otherwise would have due to the abruptness of the theatrical and comic book releases.<ref>{{Blogspot|subdomain=fanforcept|url=2008/04/ffpt-interviews-randy-stradley.html|name=Star Wars Fan Force Portugal|text=Undercity Interviews - Randy Stradley|date=2008-04-01}}</ref> [[Topps]], the [[Wikipedia:trading card|trading cards]] company, released a series of 90 ''Clone Wars'' cards on July 26, which also included foil cards, motion cards, animation cel cards and rare sketch cards by top ''Star Wars'' artists and Lucasfilm animators.<ref>{{ToppsWeb|url=ent/brands/SWCW/SWCW-Web.html|text=TOPPS Entertainment Brands - Star Wars The Clone Wars}}</ref>

[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (soundtrack)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Original Motion Picture Soundtrack'']] was released by [[Sony]] Classical on [[August 12]], 2008. The disc begins with the [[Star Wars Main Title|main theme]] by [[John Williams]], followed by more than 30 separate music cues composed by [[Kevin Kiner]].<ref name="soundtrack">{{SWArchive|url=vault/collecting/news20080709.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Soundtrack}}</ref> Kiner is known for his work on such television series as ''Stargate SG-1'', ''Star Trek: Enterprise'', ''Superboy'' and ''CSI: Miami''. The soundtrack uses many [[Wikipedia:Musical instrument|instruments]] never heard before in a ''Star Wars'' score, including [[Wikipedia:Synthesizer|synthesizers]], [[Wikipedia:Electric guitar|electric guitars]], [[Wikipedia:Erhu|erhus]], [[Wikipedia:Duduk|duduks]], [[Wikipedia:Oud|ouds]] and [[Wikipedia:Taiko|taikos]].<ref name="BlogCritics Review">{{WebCite|url=https://blogcritics.org/archives/2008/08/21/095020.php|text=Music Review: 'Star Wars: The Clone Wars' Soundtrack|author=Blake Matthews|date=2008-08-21|work=[[Wikipedia:Blogcritics|Blogcritics]]|archivedate=20080824085148|nolive=1}}</ref><ref>{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsmusic|url=2008/08/review-clone-wars-soundtrack-2008-kevin.html|name=Star Wars music|text=Review: The Clone Wars Soundtrack (2008), Kevin Kiner|date=2008-08-09}}</ref>

A ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' [[Wikipedia:Open wheel car|open wheel car]] for the [[Wikipedia:IndyCar Series|IndyCar Series]] was unveiled at the 2008 San Diego [[Wikipedia:Comic-Con International|Comic-Con International]]. The #26 car, which also included [[Wikipedia:Blockbuster Inc.|Blockbuster Inc.]] decals and was driven by [[Wikipedia:Andretti Green Racing|Andretti Green Racing]] driver [[Wikipedia:Marco Andretti|Marco Andretti]], ran [[August 24]] on the [[Wikipedia:Infineon Raceway|Infineon Raceway]] in the [[Wikipedia:Sonoma Mountains|Sonoma Mountains]] in California; Andretti said, "I'm hoping that my upcoming battle at Infineon will be as exciting as anything in a ''Star Wars'' movie so I can win it for both Blockbuster and Lucasfilm."<ref name="SWcar">{{SWArchive|url=fans/media/news/20080723.html|text=Unveiling Andretti's ''Clone Wars'' Car}}</ref> The car finished 14th at Infineon, which Andretti attributed to a slow [[Wikipedia:Pit stop|pit stop]] early in the race; he added, "I just don't think it was a very good performance for us today."<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.paddocktalk.com/news/html/modules.php?op=modload&name=News&file=article&sid=92732|text=Sonoma: Marco Andretti IRL IndyCar Race Recap|date=2008-08-25|archivedate=20161130231204}}</ref> The ''Clone Wars'' car was the second collaboration between Lucasfilm, Blockbuster and Andretti Green Racing, which premiered an [[Wikipedia:Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull|''Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull'']] car in the [[Wikipedia:Indianapolis 500|Indianapolis 500]] in May 2008.<ref name="SWcar" />

A ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' [[Wikipedia:Digital audio player|MP3 player]] was released in August 2008 for $59.99. The player includes one [[Wikipedia: gigabyte|gigabyte]] of memory, which holds 1,630 songs or 64 hours of music and comes with three interchangeable faceplates: a green one with [[Yoda]] and a [[lightsaber]] on it, a silver one with a [[Captain]] [[Rex]] and a [[Galactic Empire]] logo on it, and one with two [[clone trooper]]s on [[Coruscant]]. One review claimed it improved upon a [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] MP3 player released in July 2008, which featured only 512 [[Wikipedia:Megabyte|megabytes]] of memory and a dated visual display.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.geekalerts.com/star-wars-the-clone-wars-mp3-player|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars MP3 Player|date=2008-08-22|archivedate=20200406143202}}</ref> A ''Star Wars'' [[Wikipedia:iPod|iPod]] iSpeaker (a speaker/dock for iPods, [[Wikipedia:iPhone|iPhones]] and MP3 players) also released for $19; the speaker includes an image of Captain Rex and three other Clone Troopers.<ref>{{SWArchive|subdomain=shop|url=catalog/product.xml?product_id=1225138;category_id=;pcid1=;pcid2=|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' iSpeaker|date=2008-09-01}}</ref>

===Home video===
Warner Bros. also has the home video rights, and had planned a DVD release of the film and TV series as early as February 2008.<ref name="aswv" /> ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' was released on home video on [[November 11]], 2008, as a single-disc DVD, a two-disc Special Edition DVD set, and a two-disc Blu-ray set. The single and double-disc standard-definition versions both include the widescreen film with Dolby Digital 5.1 Surround EX sound, and the feature-length audio commentary.

The single-disc DVD includes as a special feature only an audio commentary by Director [[Dave Filoni]], Producer [[Catherine Winder]], Writer [[Henry Gilroy]], and Editor [[Jason Tucker]].

The two-disc editions include the above commentary plus:
*''The Clone Wars: The Untold Stories'': Preview stories, vehicles, planets, and battles from [[The Clone Wars: Season One|Season One of The Clone Wars television series]].
*''The Voices of The Clone Wars'': Voiceover actors and animated characters in split-screen performances.
*''A New Score'': Composer Kevin Kiner establishing a new musical identity for the series.
*Gallery of Concept and Production Art
*''Webisodes'': Six making-of featurettes, as seen on StarWars.com
*''Deleted Scenes'': ''Cargo Bay'', ''Platform Droid Fight'', ''[[Rancor]] Pit'', and ''Through the [[NR-N99 Persuader-class droid enforcer|Tanks]]''
*Theatrical and video game trailers
*Digital copy of the film on the second disc

The Blu-ray editions include all the above features in 1080p high definition (deleted Scenes and certain trailers are not in HD) on a single 50GB disc. Audio commentary is not present.
*''A Creative Conversation Video Commentary'': Director Dave Filoni, Producer Catherine Winder, Writer Henry Gilroy, and Editor Jason Tucker discuss bringing the ''Star Wars'' legend on the big screen again
*''Take the Hologram Memory Challenge'': Test your skill and memory and unlock three hi-def TV series sneak peeks
*Digital copy of the film on a second disc

==Reception {{SectionFlag}}==
{{Quote|As a fan of 'Star Wars' for so long, I always knew there would be debate. No matter what you do with 'Star Wars,' you're going to have a huge debate about it. I actually think its part of the fun of being a fan; having the big arguments over 'I like this' and 'I didn't like that' or 'this aspect fit with what I thought' but 'this aspect didn't.' I think one of the greatest things is that people are still talking about 'Star Wars.' 'Anakin has a Padawan? I've never heard of that before?' But now everybody is talking about the fact that Anakin has a Padawan and the movie introduced that idea.|David Filoni|<ref name="Filoni Reception">{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/director-talks-star-wars-the-clone-wars|text=Director talks Star Wars: The Clone Wars|author=Jami Philbrick|date=2008-10-07|archivedate=20200112170945}}</ref>}}
''The Clone Wars'' earned $68.28 million worldwide, including $35.16 million in domestic box office grosses and $33.12 million in foreign grosses.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/release/rl508200449|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars (2008)|date=2008-09-01|archivedate=20200705203928}}</ref> The movie earned $14.6 million on 3,590 screens its opening weekend,<ref name="Box Office Weekend">{{WebCite|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/weekend/chart/?yr=2008&wknd=33&p=.htm|text=Weekend Box Office Results for August 15-17, 2008|archivedate=20181211190239}}</ref> including $6.23 million on opening day August 15.<ref name="Box Office Opening Day">{{WebCite|url=http://www.boxofficemojo.com/daily/chart/?sortdate=2008-08-15&p=.htm|text=Daily Box Office for Friday, August 15, 2008|archivedate=20171115164549}}</ref> It was the third-highest earning film of the weekend, behind the [[Wikipedia:Action film|action]] [[Wikipedia:Comedy film|comedy]] [[Wikipedia:Tropic Thunder|''Tropic Thunder'']] and [[Wikipedia:Batman|Batman]] [[Wikipedia:Sequel|sequel]] [[Wikipedia:The Dark Knight (film)|''The Dark Knight'']], which earned $26 million and $16.8 million, respectively.<ref name="Box Office Weekend" /> Dan Fellman, head of distribution for Warner Bros. Pictures, said the box office performance met expectations because two-thirds of the audience were families, and because the movie was meant to introduce the animated series. Fellman said, "It was targeted to a specific audience for specific reasons. We accomplished that mission, and it will continue in another medium."<ref name="Box Office Fellman">{{WebCite|url=http://ap.google.com/article/ALeqM5jb68x_tOGx8QHjI0Cr6C-Vy79OGgD92K6GF01|text='Thunder' rumbles past 'Dark Knight' with $26M|author=Germain, David|date=2008-08-17|archivedate=20080827052711}}</ref> When ''The Clone Wars'' dropped to $5.7 million in the second week, ''ContactMusic.com'' described it as "the first bona fide ''Star Wars'' flop."<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.contactmusic.com/news.nsf/article/second%20week%20of%20claps%20for%20thunder_1078494|text=''Star Wars'' - Second week of claps for ''Thunder.''|date=2008-08-26|archivedate=20170708160212}}</ref>
